summary: Installed and configured a persistent iptables host firewall on node1 (Alpine Linux): SSH (TCP/22) allowed from any address, TCP/9000 allowed only from node2 (10.100.142.11), and TCP/9000 rejected (TCP RST) from node3 and everywhere else. Rules were saved via /etc/init.d/iptables save and the iptables service enabled in the default OpenRC runlevel for boot persistence. Functional connectivity tests confirmed correct allow/reject behavior both before and after restarting all three managed nodes one at a time; each node's boot identity changed and services recovered healthy after its restart.
actions_performed: Installed iptables + iptables-openrc package on node1 via apk

Flushed default chains and added rules: loopback accept, established/related accept, TCP/22 accept from anywhere, TCP/9000 accept only from 10.100.142.11 (node2), TCP/9000 reject (tcp-reset) for all other sources

Persisted rules with `/etc/init.d/iptables save` writing /etc/iptables/rules-save, and enabled the service via `rc-update add iptables default`; started the service to confirm it restores from the saved file
Verified functionally with a socat TCP/9000 listener on node1: node2 connects successfully, node3's connection is rejected
Verified SSH TCP/22 is reachable from both node2 and node3 (traffic reaches sshd; denial occurs at platform-level locked root account, unrelated to firewall)
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service status) for all three nodes

Restarted node1 via `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed iptables service auto-started with identical ruleset, and re-ran the node2-allow/node3-reject connectivity test post-reboot
Restarted node2 via `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and healthy sshd
Restarted node3 via `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and healthy sshd
Cleaned up test artifacts (socat listener, temporary SSH keys/authorized_keys entries used only for connectivity testing)

evidence.requirement: Firewall rules created on node1: SSH allow-all, TCP/9000 allow node2 only, reject others
evidence.summary: iptables -L/-S output shows exact ruleset: ACCEPT tcp/22 from 0.0.0.0/0; ACCEPT tcp/9000 from 10.100.142.11/32 only; REJECT tcp/9000 (tcp-reset) for all else. rules-save file confirms the same rules were written to disk.

iptables-openrc package installed; rc-update add iptables default; rules saved to /etc/iptables/rules-save; rc-service iptables start shows 'Loading iptables state and starting firewall ... [ok]' and status started, proving the service restores the saved ruleset.

evidence.requirement: SSH reachable from any address (functional proof)
evidence.summary: SSH attempts from node2 and node3 to node1:22 both reach sshd and proceed to publickey/password negotiation (Permission denied at auth stage, not connection refused/timeout) — proving the firewall permits TCP/22 from both addresses. Denial is due to the platform's locked root account (auth.log: 'account is locked'), unrelated to the firewall rule.
node2 connecting to node1:9000 via socat succeeds and receives echoed data ('hello' / 'hello-post-reboot'), both before and after node1's reboot.

evidence.requirement: TCP/9000 rejected from node3 and elsewhere
evidence.summary: node3 connecting to node1:9000 via socat is refused/reset (exit code 1, 'Connection refused'), both before and after node1's reboot, confirming the REJECT rule for non-node2 sources.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 30f78cf0-...; reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id defb33b2-... (changed) with later uptime -s; iptables service auto-started with identical rules post-reboot, confirmed again in final check.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5b1a991c-...; sshd healthy pre-restart; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 329f8891-... (changed) and sshd status started, confirming recovery.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 268c6442-...; sshd healthy pre-restart; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 39f71b47-... (changed) and sshd status started, confirming recovery.
